questions.html: Which among the following statements is/are CORRECT?

options.html: A heat transfer approaches a reversible process as the temperature difference between the two bodies tends to infinity.
Heat is a form of energy that is transferred across the system boundary by virtue of temperature difference between the system and its surroundings.
A heat transfer approaches a reversible process as the temperature difference between the two bodies approaches zero.
Heat transfer through a finite temperature difference is an irreversible process.

Everytime the door is opened, warm material is placed inside, introducing an average of 400 kJ, but making only a small change in the temperature of the refrigerator. The door is opened 10 times a day, and the refrigerator operates at 20% of the ideal COP. The cost of work is  per kWh. Atmosphere is at 27°C,
monthly bill for the refrigerator will be (Approx to nearest integer)

An inventor claims that he has developed a heat engine which extract 2000 kJ and 1000 kJ from reservoir at 900 K and 400 K respectively and rejects 500 kJ and 200 kJ as heat to reservoir at 200 K and 100 K respectively, which of the following statement is correct regarding heat engine?
